title: Yara and the Kitchen
premise: Yara Sterling, granddaughter of a lighthouse keeper, hides from love behind a half-finished novel and the safety of her late grandmother's crumbling seaside kitchen. When the town's literary festival assigns anonymous pen pals, she is paired with Theo Marsh, the developer whose family plans to buy and demolish the lighthouse property—neither knowing who the other is at first. Through letters that grow achingly honest, they fall for the person behind the enemy, until identities are revealed at the worst possible moment. Yara must choose between guarding her grief and saying the sentence she has rehearsed for ten years: that she is ready to belong to someone again, before the festival's closing night ends.
about_author: Jonah Montrose is a former pastry chef who traded restaurant kitchens for writing desks and now lives in a coastal town much like the one in this book. His fiction explores how the rooms we inherit shape the people we become.

chapters.title: Salt in the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She returns to the lighthouse cottage to sort her grandmother's kitchen, finding recipe cards annotated like love letters. Establishes her grief, her stalled novel, and her habit of keeping people at arm's length. Beat: tender loneliness.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The festival committee announces an anonymous pen-pal program for local writers. Yara signs up impulsively, telling herself it's research. Theo is shown briefly at the harbor office, signing the same list. Beat: cautious hope.

chapters.title: Demolition Notices
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo arrives in town representing his family's development firm, tasked with closing the lighthouse property deal. He resents the assignment but is unsettled by the cottage's beauty. Beat: reluctant intrusion.

chapters.title: First Letter
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The first anonymous letters arrive; Yara's correspondent is blunt where she expected softness. They spar on paper. She writes back sharper than she's spoken in years. Beat: unexpected spark.

chapters.title: The Man at the Bakery
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara encounters Theo in town over the last cardamom bun; sparks fly as open hostility. Neither knows the other is their pen pal. Beat: comic friction.

chapters.title: What the Kitchen Remembers
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Cooking her grandmother's fish stew, Yara remembers the summer her mother left and the sentence her grandmother made her rehearse: 'I can let someone in.' She writes it into a letter. Beat: grief surfacing.

chapters.title: Letters Without Faces
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confesses in his letter that he hates his job and the deal he's here to close. Reading the reply, he feels known for the first time in years. Beat: guarded vulnerability.

chapters.title: Survey Flags
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's survey team stakes the lighthouse grounds; Yara catches him on her property and throws him out. That night, both write letters about enemies who feel like mirrors. Beat: rising tension.

chapters.title: The Festival Opens
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The literary festival begins; Yara reads a chapter of her novel publicly and falters on a line about belonging. Theo watches, unrecognized, and is moved. Beat: public exposure of private wounds.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A rainstorm traps Yara and Theo in the bakery cellar; the hostility cracks into real conversation. They part before names or histories surface, both shaken. Beat: intimacy without identity.

chapters.title: The Recipe for Forgiving
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds his late mother's recipe box while packing his hotel room and writes to his pen pal about it. He begins drafting a proposal to preserve the lighthouse kitchen. Beat: inheritance reframed.

chapters.title: Deadline on the Deed
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara learns the sale closes the day after the festival. Panicked, she leans on her pen pal's encouragement and decides to fight the sale publicly. Beat: resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Crossed Wires
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At a festival mixer, Yara and Theo nearly exchange confessions but are interrupted by Theo's boss, who reveals Theo's surname to the room. Yara leaves without hearing Theo's denial. Beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Letter That Wasn't Sent
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara writes an angry letter to her pen pal about the developer 'Sterling's enemy,' not realizing she's describing him. Theo reads it and goes silent, unable to confess. Beat: guilt and paralysis.

chapters.title: Midnight in the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo breaks into the cottage—keys from the survey office—to photograph the kitchen for a preservation case. Yara catches him; the confrontation turns raw, and she orders him out for good. Beat: lowest point approaching.

chapters.title: Revelations
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The festival's pen-pal reveal night arrives: envelopes with names. Yara and Theo discover they've been writing to each other all along. She walks into the storm; he lets her go, then decides he won't. Beat: climax of identity.

chapters.title: The Public Hearing
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At the sale hearing, Theo betrays his firm, presenting a preservation proposal funded by his own inheritance and confessing his pen-pal identity publicly. Beat: sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the festival's closing night, before the whole town, Yara stands at the lighthouse rail and says the sentence she has rehearsed for a decade: 'I am ready to let someone in.' Beat: emotional climax.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara and Theo reconcile in the kitchen, cooking her grandmother's stew together. The sale is halted; the cottage becomes a writers' retreat with Theo's name on the deed beside hers. Beat: warmth.

chapters.title: Last Letter, First Name
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo writes one final anonymous-style letter and hand-delivers it, signing his name. Yara reads it aloud in the kitchen. Beat: quiet joy.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Kitchen Table
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. One year later, the retreat's first cohort gathers at the kitchen table; Yara's novel is finished, its last line the rehearsed sentence. Theo sets down two cups of coffee. Beat: belonging earned.

chapters.title: Coda: Tide Chart
chapters.summary: Dual POV, brief alternating sections. A short coda of the couple's letters bound into a booklet sold at the festival, ending with the tide chart Yara's grandmother kept and one new annotation in two hands. Beat: inheritance continued.
